steps.say: Verbs can show when something happens: in the past, the present or the future.
steps.show: I played. I play. I will play.

steps.say: Many past tense verbs end in -ed.
Some verbs change in a different way. We have to learn these ones.
steps.show: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw

steps.say: The present tense is for now, or for things that happen often. Add -s after he, she or it.
Use will with a verb to talk about the future.
Time words help you choose the tense: yesterday, every day and tomorrow.
steps.show: Yesterday I swam. Tomorrow I will swim.

options.why: Makes is the present tense. Last week is in the past.
Will make is for the future.
Making needs a helper word, like was making.

hints: Last week is in the past.
Make is irregular. It does not take -ed.
check.explanation: Last week is in the past, and the past tense of make is made.

check.prompt:
Write the missing word to show the future.
Next year, I ___ be nine.
hints: Next year is in the future.
One small word goes in front of a verb to show the future.
check.explanation: We use will to talk about the future: Next year, I will be nine.
